order.liveRuns: MSFT ×2 and AZN ×1, budgeted at £8 each

measurement.issue1Test: The journey harness (tests/e2e/journey.py plus audit/smoke.py's screenshot scan, both on the fake scene at £0) writes six numbers with stated bounds, and ISSUE 1 is fixed when all six clear: (a) every row of the committed dead-end inventory has a browser-proved, labelled forward control, and zero stopped states offer none — three rows start red by design; (b) zero UUIDs and zero pages whose visible text names a CLI command, across every page the journey visits and every StepPaused message in src/; (c) at most one value the operator must supply or amend at the assumptions gate on a USD run, against 2 on MSFT and 5 on AZN; (d) three of three live runs in the M2 window reach an approved, rendered report with no terminal use and no rescue, against three of six in September; (e) a readable, figure-bearing surface exists on screen at the moment the draft step finishes, with every unwritten section named as still being written and no approval control on it; (f) the operator walks §4.4's six by-hand checks and the testing-by-hand scorecard with no [B] row failing. (f) is the only one a harness cannot score, and it is deliberately the last word.
measurement.issue2Test: The blind judge comparison, re-run through a coded harness with neutral identically-shaped document paths, a seeded A/B assignment and the identity guess recorded. September's true baseline, recomputed from judges/reads.json with the A/B swap on the azn round honoured: 54 dimension votes across nine comparisons — console 51, equal 3, platform 0; focus questions 1 yes / 17 partly / 9 no for the platform against 6 yes / 21 partly / 0 no for the console; would-act 'no' on 9 of 9 platform reads. ISSUE 2 is fixed when, at M2: (1) PRIMARY — better_on_verifiability names the platform in at least 4 of 6 comparisons, against 0 of 9; (2) better_answers_the_brief is not a clean loss — at least 3 of 6 name the platform or equal, against 0 of 9; (3) at least 2 of 6 platform reads move would_act_on_it off 'no'; (4) across 18 focus-question readings, zero score 'no' and at least three score 'yes'; (5) no judge's first_thing_to_check names an internal contradiction, and no decisive field contains 'contradict', 'cannot be compared to anything' or 'no view'; (6) the published documents contain no figure name+period with two values, no sentence asserting a figure is unavailable that another section prints, and zero occurrences of 'Escalated for human decision'. If the judges identify which document is machine-assembled in 8 or 9 of 9, the round is reported as format-confounded and a narrower instrument is run — the three focus-question answers alone, footnote markers stripped, asked which answers the question better.
measurement.target: Verifiability is the bar, because it is the one dimension the platform exists for and the one where the evidence is already on disk: at least 4 of 6 blind comparisons naming the platform, against 0 of 9 today. Beside it, three supporting numbers fixed now rather than after the result is known: not a clean loss on the brief (≥3 of 6 platform-or-equal), at least 2 of 6 reads off 'would not act', and zero 'no' answers across 18 focus-question readings. ISSUE 1's bar is binary and offline: the journey harness green on every dead-end inventory row, zero terminal references and zero UUIDs in visible text, ≤1 hand-typed assumption on a USD run, and 3 of 3 M2 runs reaching an approved report without rescue. Explicitly NOT a target, because the record shows it is already met and cannot signal a fix: 'an investment view is stated and argued 3 of 3' — azn2 scored exactly that and still lost 3 of 3. That measure moves to the no-regression list, alongside 0 contradicted numerals, 100% citation verification, every blocking metric at its threshold and every run at or under £10.
permanentMetrics: figure_agreement_across_sections — BLOCKING, but through the gate's own refusal path and not through eval/metrics.py, whose rows are scores and never a pause

filing_agreement — the numeral matcher against the filed bytes, moved into src/aer/eval/ with the artefact read in the service layer; ADVISORY until a mutation corpus measures the recall the audit never did, and never blocking on a corpus it was calibrated to zero on

the completeness readout — nine named headline figures present or withheld with reasons, built from the run's own rows rather than substring matches; a READOUT on the acceptance check and the final gate, never blocking, because ADR 0066 settled that withholding can be the right answer and F-25 shows what happens when a check judges the platform's own withheld-figure note

reader_verifiability — distinct citation targets, the share of evidence footnotes resolving to a machine endpoint, and the share openable at all; advisory, back-tested against the five committed reports
brief_coverage — focus questions carrying no cited figure; a gate-2 DISPLAY, with the actual refusal living in the answers-block emitter that declines to render an empty entry

view_stated and self_consistency_of_absence — advisory, the second specified structurally (the intersection of the concepts the document publishes as figures and those a section's claims assert absent) rather than lexically, which requires an absence assertion to be a declared field first

NOT the run-to-run variance comparison — it needs two runs of the same subject and one of its inputs is an operator-confirmed assumption, so a 'failure' can be ADR 0046 working; it stays an on-demand instrument in audit/, run free over the M2 MSFT pair
NOT any model judge at run time — a model scoring a model's prose, unreplayable, and billed on every run
measurement.reRunPlan: Two rounds. M1 (after step 9, roughly session 45): two platform runs — MSFT and AZN — at £8 budgeted each, reusing all three September console notes, with twelve judged reads and six blind comparisons. £21 total. This is the decision point: it tests the plan's thesis before the expensive acquisition work, and if verifiability has not flipped the thesis is wrong and the remaining plan should be re-written rather than continued. M2 (after step 16): three platform runs — MSFT twice, the second doubling as the refresh use case and giving the variance comparison free, plus AZN once — reusing the same baselines, with eighteen reads and nine comparisons, the journey harness, and the three permanent readouts reported beside the judges' votes. £31.50. Baselines are reused deliberately, not to save money but because a stale console note is a lower bound on the console: if the platform still loses against it the result is conclusive. One fresh MSFT baseline (£7.63) is bought only if the platform wins, and only to check the win survives a same-week comparator. Before judging, confirm no new annual or interim filing for either subject has landed between the baseline's date and the run's; if one has, that subject's baseline is re-bought rather than reused. The asymmetry created by ADR 0110 — the platform is stamped with today and the console notes are dated 11–12 September 2026 — is reported in the protocol, and 'recent developments' is reported separately from the other five dimensions. Do not restore an operator-typed as-of date to make measurement cheaper; ADR 0110 refused that field because a wrong date fails silently.

operatorDecisions: A bank's revenue — derive it (net interest income + non-interest income, a traced calculation), withhold it (an ASC 606 component is not a total where a larger non-606 revenue line exists for the same period, at the parse layer), or leave it and accept that no bank can be researched. RECOMMENDATION: withhold first, then derive on top — and the ordering is load-bearing rather than stylistic, because seven of the eleven impossible relations are quarterly and analyse_company builds annual statements only, so a calculation-layer fix alone clears four of eleven and gate 2 stays refused. The definition is verified, not assumed: the FY2021–FY2023 splice reproduces exactly against the archived companyfacts (3,825+2,167=5,992; 5,822+2,357=8,179; 7,115+2,528=9,643, delta zero in all three years). Run that splice before spending anything.

Which price-derived figures may appear in an exported report — market capitalisation, enterprise value, multiples and implied up/downside only; those plus the raw close; or neither. RECOMMENDATION: the first, and note honestly that market capitalisation divided by the filed share count gives the reader the price to two decimals anyway, so 'print the capitalisation but not the price' is a distinction without much difference. The genuinely different option is 'neither', and 'neither' is what produced eight of nine comparisons saying the per-share outputs cannot be compared to anything. This is your licence determination, not an engineering question: your own note at fetch/policy.py:176-192 already permits derived figures and the render boundary has not caught up, which is itself a defect to close either way.

Whose view the report states — the operator's own at approval, a model role over a frozen draft, a mechanical derivation, or none. RECOMMENDATION: yours, recorded as an ADR 0102 judgement with a holder, two clocks, a basis that cannot be blank, falsifiers and supersession, displayed and never cited. It is not investment advice because nobody is advising anybody; it is your own research journal, which is what this tool is. A model-authored rating I would refuse outright: `rating` is the first entry in RESERVED_OUTPUT_FIELDS precisely because a one-word label with no holder, no time and no stated basis is the closest thing this platform can produce to regulated advice, and permitting it through the built-in door while refusing it through the skill door would make invariant 7 a statement about file formats. Settle reports.confidence in the same record.

Peer multiples — acquire eight peers' companyfacts, drop the multiples from the eighteen-section spine, or keep proposing peers and say the table is structurally empty. RECOMMENDATION: acquire, but only after the seeding measurement, and note that the subject's own P/E and EV/EBITDA are already computed on every run and cost nothing to print — that alone may be enough, and M1 will say. Fix the wording in an hour regardless of the answer: the report today says the peers were 'excluded', which reads as a verdict on the peers rather than a statement about this tool. Acquiring re-creates exactly the condition ADR 0061 was written to stop, so the scope test ships first.

The evidence tier ceiling — leave every built-in section at T4, raise to T5 on named outward-facing sections, raise everywhere a model writes, or a per-run operator switch. RECOMMENDATION: raise on recent_developments, catalysts, industry_landscape and growth_outlook only, by publishing a new version row rather than an in-place merge (an in-place merge retroactively changes the policy a finished run was drafted under, and draft_replay reads the pinned policy); requires_primary and min_sources do not move; and claim-level tier marking ships in the same change or the reader cannot tell which sentences got looser. Note the record cuts both ways: the console's advantage here rested on a Substack, CNN and btw.media, and every judge docked it for exactly that.

Whether to build a UK acquisition path at all. RECOMMENDATION: no. It is seven to ten sessions, two ADRs, a live-register probe and delivers annual-only, months-stale, peerless evidence for a company whose US-listed compatriots already work. Instead spend a session and a half: refuse LSE at request creation for £0 instead of at £0.55, and fix the message that tells an operator asking for AstraZeneca that AstraZeneca is 'a different company'. Narrow the product's claim to 'a filer with the SEC'. Only you know whether your own universe is UK-listed — if it is, this recommendation inverts and the UK path becomes the plan's largest item.

Cost published inside a step, or the worst case reserved up front (amends ADR 0016 either way, or not at all). RECOMMENDATION: reservation. Publishing early is not implementable as the diagnosis describes it — Cost.agent_run_id foreign-keys an agent_runs row that is still uncommitted on the step's session, so early publication means publishing agent_runs early too, which is a much larger amendment. Reservation needs no ADR and its inputs already exist, because ADRs 0052/0053 already require per-step estimates.

A superseding decision at a gate whose payload has moved — narrow (admitted only when the recorded approval matches neither the seal nor the live page, which is exactly the state with no exit today) or wide (whenever the payload moved). RECOMMENDATION: narrow. The wide rule can rescue an operator who simply changed their mind, which is a different product. The ADR must also say what a superseding decision does to the frozen seal, because recording AMENDED against the live page puts the run in the branch whose message names aer reseal.

The sector gate's third answer, and whether the four non-blocking profiles should stop a run at all. RECOMMENDATION: build the third answer, scoped to the four blocking profiles only (bank, insurer, REIT, pre-revenue biotech), with a closed list, a mandatory reason, Decision.AMENDED carrying the corrected payload and its own hash re-checked at the deep guard. Amending away from a blocking profile is the permissive direction and needs the typed reason and the disclosure. On the second half: no — keep F-23's narrowing permanently, because a profile that blocks nothing changes only which warnings a report carries.

The re-measurement budget and the bar, chosen now rather than after the result is known. RECOMMENDATION: £21 at M1 and £31.50 at M2, with verifiability ≥4 of 6 as the primary bar and 'not a clean loss on the brief' as the split target. If you would rather a weaker bar, choose it in the pre-registration document, not afterwards.

Whether to spend £4 measuring a quick run. RECOMMENDATION: yes, once, at M1. AnalysisMode.QUICK exists, drops nine of eighteen sections and scales budgets to 0.6, and has never been run, costed or judged. It is the cheapest existing route to a shorter document and the question it raises — is a nine-section note that keeps the summary, thesis, statements, valuation and risks better than an eighteen-section one that lost six blind comparisons — is the right one to put to the judges.

The scale of the plan itself. RECOMMENDATION: commit to steps 1–10 (about 45 sessions, about £29 of live spend) and make everything after M1 conditional on what M1 measures. Ninety verified findings do not compress into a small plan, but they do compress into a plan with a stop point, and this one has one.
newAdrs: The view a report states is the operator's own, recorded at approval as an ADR 0102 judgement with a holder, a time, a basis that cannot be blank and its falsifiers — displayed, never cited, never written by a model or a rule; and reports.confidence is settled in the same record.

ADR 0034, amended: the assembler accepts a comps table and the provider's licence flag decides rather than the signature — the type still decides, the decision just moves; and the shareable type carries the operator-confirmed peers' names and rationales.

ADR 0030, amended: which price-derived figures may appear in an exported artefact — a market capitalisation, an enterprise value, a multiple and an implied up or downside may; the series itself and any chart of it may not.

ADR 0058, amended: a section may ask for dimensioned facts by axis, and the axis and member are carried wherever such a figure is shown — the Decision names section evidence packs explicitly, so this is a recorded change and not a wiring detail.

A bank's revenue, in two halves: an ASC 606 component is not a total where the filer reports a larger revenue line outside ASC 606's scope for the same period (a statement about the taxonomy, at the parse layer, needing no classification); and a bank's revenue is net interest income plus non-interest income (a modelling definition, in aer.calc, where a reported total always wins and a single present component never derives).

ADR 0039 and ADR 0095, amended: code adjudicates a challenge's arithmetic premise and never its argument; materiality follows severity AND a surviving premise; an approved report carries no undecided challenge; and ADR 0091 is amended so the operator's own settlement may change the appendix after the revise seal, the reseal being what keeps the approval honest.
A cross-section figure disagreement refuses the run at gate 2 through the gate's own blocking path — the eval rows are scores and never a pause, and this check is not a score.

A decision may be superseded exactly when the payload it was taken on no longer exists, recorded as AMENDED beside the original rather than replacing it, and what that does to the frozen seal and to the replace-not-append rule evaluate_run documents today.

ADR 0029, amended: a classification may be corrected by the person who confirms it; the correction carries a mandatory reason and its own re-checked payload hash, sets the mandate, and a correction towards the permissive answer is disclosed in the report.

ADR 0059, third amendment: peer acquisition returns now the price feed exists — resolved, fetched, scoped to the peer's own company row under ADR 0061, no excerpt location, no segment sweep, and a peer figure still never cited in prose.

An accession is a set of documents, not one: acquisition fetches a filing's typed exhibits as well as its primary document, which ones, how each is dated and tiered, and what may and may not be read out of an exhibit's tables (a figure still comes from XBRL, never from an excerpt).

A named outward-facing section may read secondary reporting as corroboration and never as sole support for a figure — requires_primary and min_sources unmoved — and every claim resting on one says so to the reader on the page, printing the evidence tier with the recorded tier beside it when they differ.

ADR 0109, amended: a numeric claim naming a fact is checked against that fact's value, whether the figure is a fact or a calculation; and, extending ADR 0097, a figure's scale word is part of the figure, so the reading ladder narrows to the readings the writer's own words admit.

A standing operator assumption is a stored proposal with its own justification and date, re-proposed into every run and confirmed at the gate like any other — and never held in macro_observations, which ADR 0082 reserves for sourced, dated published observations.
What a scenario holds fixed (§8 item 8): whether a scenario overriding beta or the risk-free rate recomputes the WACC, and that the answer is stated on the rendered scenario row.

ADR 0016, amended — only if reservation is refused: money is published when it is spent rather than when the step that spent it commits, covering agent_runs as well as costs, because the cost row's foreign key requires it.
notDoing: A news pipeline. T5 is admitted as corroboration on four named outward-facing sections and never as sole support for a figure — which is the rule SourceTier's own docstring already states. The console's recency advantage came from CNN, Robinhood, a Substack and btw.media, and every judge docked it for exactly that. Chasing it would invert the thing the platform exists to be, and the honest gain is in the filings the run should already be reading: the results-release exhibit and the interim 6-K.

Use case 7, research under time pressure. A tool that asks a human to approve six gates cannot beat a tool that asks nothing, on minutes, ever. The free concurrency fixes take machine time from 26–37 minutes to roughly 19–22 and the six decisions remain. What is fixed instead is the 22 minutes of silence in which nothing readable exists — and two surfaces that would fix it are already built and linked from nowhere. Say so on the request form and in the product documentation rather than pretending the gap is closable.

The UK acquisition path — the Companies House adapter, the iXBRL facts parser, the presentation locator, the UK SIC scheme, the point-in-time anchor. Seven to ten sessions, two ADRs, a live-register probe whose premise nobody has tested, delivering annual-only, months-stale, peerless evidence. Instead: refuse LSE at request creation, fix the refusal message, correct the knowledge map, and narrow the product's claim to 'a filer with the SEC'. Revisit only if the operator's own universe is UK-listed.

Phase 6 — authentication, inbound rate limiting, a production deployment story. Gated on intent to leave one machine, and neither issue creates that intent: this is one operator, one laptop, one report at a time.

Everything on the roadmap's Decided-against list, and in particular a model-authored rating or confidence. RESERVED_OUTPUT_FIELDS exists to keep exactly that out through the skill door; letting it in through the built-in door would make invariant 7 a statement about file formats rather than about ratings.

Any model-judge metric at run time. It would be a model scoring a model's prose — unreplayable, billed on every run, and refused by ADR 0035's record requirement and by the cost invariant. The judge panel stays an occasional acceptance harness under audit/, never a gate.

A quarterly statement pass. Tempting, because it is the only route to the bank's seven quarterly plausibility findings from the calculation layer — and it is a far larger change than the revenue question, which reaches gate 2 without it.
P/FFO, REIT specialist multiples, and the insurer and holding-company profiles' unwritten metrics. No REIT has been researched and nothing would exercise them.
Raising MAX_PARALLEL_NODES. The engine refuses it by construction and calls it part of the cost model; the draft fan-out is the bound to move, and only after sibling spend is visible.

Renaming the six recorded `multiple` calculations. It moves a replay boundary and would put the audit's '3,335 rows replayed with zero divergence' claim on a different code version, for an evidence-labelling problem that is fixed by surfacing the parameters already recorded.

A magnitude-based subtotal heuristic on the segment axis. Any company with one segment above half of revenue would meet it, so the rule would silently delete the largest genuine segment — a chart whose bars are all stored facts and whose composition is a deterministic fiction, which no check would catch.

Chasing peer multiples through anything other than acquiring peer filings. There is no third way: either eight peers' companyfacts are fetched under the ADR 0061 guard, or the report says structurally that this tool does not acquire peer financials. Both are honest; the current wording is not, and changes in an hour either way.

risks.risk: The fixes land and the blind comparison still does not flip. This is not hypothetical: AZN #2 was exactly that experiment — the valuation restored, 831 calculations where there had been 152, view_stated 3/3 and argued 3/3 — and it changed no verdict, with all three comparisons still choosing the console.
risks.mitigation: M1 exists for this and is deliberately early and cheap (£21, two runs, after roughly 45 sessions). Its primary bar is verifiability, which is the one dimension where the evidence is already on disk and where I would predict a clean flip. If verifiability has not moved at M1, the plan's organising thesis is wrong and the remaining sixty sessions should be re-planned rather than continued — that is the honest use of a measurement gate.

risks.risk: The judges are one model sampled three times. Across nine comparisons and six dimensions the vote was 51–3–0 and the three lenses agreed on would-act 9 times out of 9. That unanimity is either a very strong signal about the documents or an artefact of three prompts sharing a prior, and nothing in the record distinguishes them.
risks.mitigation: Include one discriminating pair in each round where the lenses should disagree — the platform's MSFT report against the platform's own AZN report — and check that they do. Report the identity-guess hit rate. Serve both documents from neutral, identically shaped paths. And keep §4.4's operator read as the last word, because no harness settles whether the person with money at stake would act.

risks.risk: The cross-section reconciliation check fires constantly on true positives and blocks every run, turning a quality gate into an obstacle the operator learns to wave through.
risks.mitigation: Ship the deterministic half offline against the five stored documents first and count exactly what it would have refused, before it can refuse anything. Scope the refusal to name+period exact collisions and explicit negative assertions only. Land it advisory for one live run before it blocks.

risks.risk: Three diagnosis items assume a 'the run stops at gate 2' mechanism that does not exist — _validate's own docstring is 'scores, never a pause', and msft2 reached AWAITING_APPROVAL with presentation_integrity failing.
risks.mitigation: Build the blocking path once, in step 3, before anything routes through it. Every test that asserts a refusal is written against that one mechanism, and each is shown failing against HEAD first.

risks.risk: Peer acquisition re-creates ADR 0061's live failure — the Amazon note that cited Walmart, Alibaba, eBay, JD.com, MercadoLibre and Target as its own evidence.
risks.mitigation: The standing scope test (every fact id in every built-in section's pack resolves to the subject's company_id, and no source id names a quarantined document) is written and green in step 3, long before any peer acquisition merges. The seeding runs in step 15 exercise it with real peer rows before the in-run acquisition is built at all.

risks.risk: Printing a market capitalisation breaches the EODHD agreement, and several WS2 items are designed on the assumption that it does not. The codebase itself is split: the policy flag says derived figures are publishable and the render boundary enforces the older posture.
risks.mitigation: Step 1 re-reads the executed agreement and writes the answer into one place everything reads, before any render change. If the answer is no, the price-position items are dropped and the plan states plainly that the product cannot position a per-share output — which is a change to what it claims to be, and should be said as one.

risks.risk: The plan is roughly ninety-five sessions and four to five months of solo work; appetite runs out somewhere in the middle and the result is a half-finished platform with a half-finished plan.
risks.mitigation: Steps 1–10 are a complete, self-contained plan with its own measurement (about 45 sessions, £29 of live spend) and every step after M1 is explicitly conditional. Each workstream has an exit criterion that can be claimed on its own. Nothing later depends on something earlier being incomplete.

risks.risk: A live run in a measurement round fails and the money is wasted. The audit's own record is three of six runs reaching an approved report.
risks.mitigation: audit/smoke.py runs the whole workflow on the fake scene for £0 before a penny moves, as it did in September. WS6's dead-end and recovery work lands before M2, so a stranded M2 run has an exit. M1's two runs carry the risk knowingly, and the protocol's anti-gaming clause means a badly-reading run is judged rather than discarded.

risks.risk: Re-measuring the metrics after revise needs a deterministic entry point out of evaluate_run that may not exist — its own docstring names LLM assists inside it, and its signature documents a batch path for advisory questions.
risks.mitigation: Establish whether the assists are separable as the first half-hour of that item. If they are not, the carve-out is the work and the estimate doubles; say so before starting rather than discovering it. Note that _revise already re-runs validate_draft per revised section, so the draft-time rules are not stale — only the gate-2 metric rows are, which narrows the item usefully.

risks.risk: The audit's five runs no longer exist in a live database, which four acceptance criteria and a great deal of free offline verification quietly assume. The committed evidence is JSON exports and there is no aer import-run.
risks.mitigation: Establish this in step 1, before anything is scheduled against it. If the store is gone, one early MSFT run (£7) re-establishes a replay subject and the offline acceptance criteria are rewritten against synthetic fixtures — and the plan's spend rises by that £7, not by more.

risks.risk: WS7's reach items each add fetches, extractions, excerpts and in one case a nineteenth section, against a run that already takes 26–37 minutes of machine time and asks for six decisions — the axis use case 7 already fails on.
risks.mitigation: State the word budget as a hard number in the recent-developments migration. Measure expected run cost and step time after the whole workstream before it merges — msft2's draft step was £2.31 for eighteen sections, so a nineteenth is £0.13–0.15 against a £10 cap, immaterial on money and not on time. WS6's concurrency work lands first so the time budget has headroom to spend.

risks.risk: The plan's own thesis — that the platform computes more than it prints — recurs in whatever is built next, because nothing structurally prevents it. Six complete, tested modules are already called from nowhere but tests.
risks.mitigation: Three standing tests in step 3 and step 17: the route-reachability test over the shell registry's UNLISTED set, the implemented-and-uncalled register over __all__ exports, and the computed-but-unprinted test over every distinct calculation name a run records. Each fails the build rather than waiting for an audit.

plans.totalEffort: Roughly 95 sessions — about four to five months at a session a day for one person driving an AI coding session — of which steps 1–10 (about 45 sessions) are a complete plan with its own measurement and its own stop point. By workstream: WS1 agreement 8–10; WS2 print-what-exists 11–13; WS3 checkable export 5–7; WS4 the view 5–6; WS5 the bank 7–9; WS6 the operator's path 16–19; WS7 reach 18–22; WS8 guards and integrity 9–11; WS9 measurement 9–11. About sixty of those sessions are connecting, correcting or printing something that already exists and is already tested, which is why the estimate is large but the risk is not.
firstThreeThings: Commit the pre-registered targets and the re-measurement protocol at a hash that predates any code change, with every September value written beside the threshold it must beat — 54 dimension votes (console 51, equal 3, platform 0); focus questions 1 yes / 17 partly / 9 no; would-act 'no' on 9 of 9; verifiability 0 of 9 to the platform. In the same sitting, settle two facts the whole plan rests on: whether the audit's five runs still exist in a live database, and what the executed EODHD agreement actually permits in an exported artefact — written into one place everything reads, because fetch/policy.py and render/document.py currently disagree about it. Without the pre-registration the re-measurement becomes an exercise in finding the dimension that improved, and the platform has 779 clean figures available to quote on any day.

Port F-27's already-written, already-reviewed, already-tested calculation query from services/red_team.py:343-374 into gather_evidence at sections/evidence.py:580-588 — one row per (name, case) at its newest period, sensitivity cells excluded, calculations bounded separately from facts, the period carried on every entry — and add a reserved floor for the figure set the front page actually prints. One session, no ADR. This single ORDER BY period_end DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 40, against a valuation whose every output carries period = None, is why the Executive Summary says 'no valuation output, no discount rate and no peer multiple' eleven lines under a front page printing WACC 9.3% and Value per share $485.29. It is the largest single cause of the self-contradiction that seven of nine judges decided on, and the answer is already written one layer over.

Change assemble_document's comps parameter from `WithheldComps | None` to `CompsTable | WithheldComps | None` and have the caller pass for_audience(SHAREABLE) — persisting the calculation ids in the comps outcome so each multiple footnotes the way the DCF's figures do, and changing render/html.py and render/summary.py in the same commit, or the exported artefact a reader actually receives is unchanged. Every run since the audit began computed the subject's P/E at 27.43x and EV/EBITDA at 18.93x, each a traced calculation replayed with zero divergence; the only thing stopping them reaching a reader is a type signature enforcing a licence position the operator reversed on 2026-08-09, which CompsTable.for_audience already honours and the render boundary never asks. It turns two of the six checklist rows the platform lost into present-sourced, and it is the plainest possible demonstration of what is wrong with this product.

fatalFlaws: Not fatal, but load-bearing and unexamined: almost every exit criterion in this plan is 'replay/re-render msft1, azn2 and mtb from their own stored rows', and nothing in the plan establishes that the audit's five run databases and artefact store still exist. Plans 2 and 4 both raise this as a step-1 question. If that store is gone, the plan's entire offline-proof economy (steps 1-6, 8, 9, 10 all at spendGbp 0) collapses into paid live runs and the £43 becomes £80+.

The bank (F-24) — the one blocking finding the audit left open, and the reason an entire subject class produces no report at all — is an optional branch inside step 8 gated on an operator decision. The plan's own analysis of it is correct (withhold at the parse layer first, because seven of eleven findings are quarterly), but correct analysis filed under 'optional' is not a fix.
whatToGraft: The step-7 LIVE STEER and its pre-registered reading. £10.50 after six offline steps, on azn2 — the one subject where this thesis has already been half-tested and failed — with three named outcomes written down in advance and a stated re-ordering if the thesis is wrong. This is the best decision gate in the four plans and the single thing I would keep above everything else.

The causal ordering argument itself: keyhole → stop contradicting → anchor → view, with azn2 (view_stated 3/3, argued 3/3, still lost 3/3) used as the evidence for why the view is fourth and not first. Nobody else defends their ordering this well.
The ADR discipline: fourteen ADRs each naming which recorded decision it amends, four flagged as 'must exist before their code', plus the conditional ones 'named so they are not forgotten'.
The three built-in stopping points (after step 6 the document has a spine; after step 9 the evidence is legible; after step 11 the prose argues), each leaving a better product than today.

Routing every refusal through the FINAL gate's evidence rule rather than eval/metrics.py, and gating the new cross-section check on two consecutive clean live runs so it cannot strand the programme's own re-runs.

fatalFlaws: No fatal flaw. Two real costs: 65 sessions is four to five months of solo work and the ISSUE-2 verdict arrives at step 15 of 15, which is a long time to wait to learn whether the document work moved anything (partly answered by its own £11 mid-point signal at step 9).

Its own ordering contradicts its own advice: the F-27 evidence port is one session, no ADR, no spend, and is the defect every judge named first — its firstThreeThings ranks it third of three, but the running order puts it at step 6 behind roughly fourteen sessions. Take its advice, not its order.
whatToGraft: The bank at step 2, before anything else that touches the document. Its correction to the audit's sizing is the sharpest technical argument in the four plans: a calculation-layer derivation clears 4 of 11 findings and gate 2 still refuses, because seven of the eleven impossible relations are quarterly and analyse_company builds annual statements only — so the withhold-at-the-parse-layer ordering is load-bearing, not stylistic, and the FY2021-23 splice is a free offline gate that must pass before any code.

The replay-subject question as a step-1 deliverable: settle whether `aer replay-draft` can still reach those five job ids, because that answer decides whether the programme costs £34 or £60. This is the dependency the winning plan does not examine.

The 'replay-first rule' written into CONTRIBUTING.md: a document change ships only with an offline proof (re-render, replay-draft, rehearse-section); a live run is spent only on what no stored run can exercise. That rule is what makes any of these plans affordable.

The dead-end inventory derived from runs/console.html's own panels as well as from §5 — including the failed-step fallback reading 'The worker terminal holds the full record' and the `remedy` branch that deliberately offers no forward control. The richer inventory is the better ISSUE-1 test.
The observation that the re-seal action is a prerequisite of the re-measure action (re-scoring always moves the live payload off the frozen seal) — the diagnosis has that dependency backwards.
'NOT NEEDED, and worth recording as such so nobody drafts one' — the list of changes that explicitly do not need an ADR. That saves real sessions.

fatalFlaws: FATAL on price. £182.50 total against a £100 ceiling of which £63.32 is already spent, asking me to raise CEILING_GBP to £190 and fund five measurement events (18-24 judged reads each) for a one-person, one-machine personal research tool. Plan 1 answers the same question for £43 and Plan 2 for £60. Attribution at tranche resolution is a nice-to-have; it is not worth four times the money.

FATAL on order, from this seat. By its own admission fourteen sessions and £7.50 pass before a single product defect is fixed, and its own risk register concedes 'an operator watching may reasonably ask what they bought'. Meanwhile the two cheapest judge-visible changes on the board — the F-27 evidence port and the comps parameter type — are one session each and sit at steps 8 and 12.

85-95 sessions and 25 new or amended ADRs, four of which gate work that cannot start before they exist. An ADR ledger that size is itself a delivery risk for one person driving AI sessions; it is process I would not finish.
whatToGraft: THE CALIBRATION ROUND. Re-judge September's committed corpus with the newly coded panel and require it to reproduce the recorded per-comparison verdicts before any later round is believed. This is the single best measurement idea in any of the four plans: it costs one sitting and £7.50, and finding out the instrument is wrong then rather than after a £31.50 round is exactly the right trade. No other plan has it.

'The four counters that count the wrong thing' as a one-sitting early step: the turnover guard querying `total_assets` where the canonical concept is `assets` (verified — the branch is unreachable from the gate), the price step reporting absence when it means no new bars, the gate-1 estimate summing overlapping steps, and the two docstrings whose counts the code contradicts. The framing is right: fix what makes the instrument measure a bug before you build the instrument.

The one-page note recording what can actually stop a run — the FINAL gate's evidence rule, the degradation path, and the fact that an eval row cannot. Eleven diagnosis items propose refusals through a mechanism that does not exist; writing this down once prevents eleven tests that cannot pass.
The requirement that every acceptance criterion naming a refusal must also name the code path that refuses.

The discriminating pair in every judging round (the platform's MSFT against the platform's own AZN) to test whether the three lenses ever disagree — and the honesty to report the panel as 'one opinion sampled three times' if they never do.

The operator's FIRST-named issue is 'the system is not user ready in many ways'; the harness that proves it is free and runs offline on the fake scene at £0; and this plan makes it wait roughly three months behind the second issue. That is the wrong half to defer.

95 sessions and £108 is the second-largest programme here. The bounded phase 1 (steps 1-10, ~45 sessions, ~£29) genuinely helps — but ISSUE 1 sits outside that bound, so the bounded offer only buys half the operator's request.
whatToGraft: THE FRAMING, wholesale. 'The two issues are one issue: the platform computes, stores, hashes and verifies far more than it ever shows anybody.' I checked it and it is literally true — create_scenario, set_override, margin_bridge, MacroClient and override_citation have no caller anywhere in src/ outside their own __all__. This is the version of the work that is legible to me as the person paying for it, and it correctly predicts that most of the plan is hours-to-a-session rather than architecture.

Settling the ADR 0030 / EODHD contradiction in step 1, in ONE place everything reads, before any render change. `fetch/policy.py:192` sets derived_figures_publishable=True and `render/document.py:436` still enforces the pre-amendment posture — the codebase disagrees with itself, and this is the only plan that refuses to design three workstream items on top of that. If the answer is 'no', it says plainly that the product cannot position a per-share output and that this is a change to what it claims to be.

The three standing tests: route-reachability over the shell registry's UNLISTED set (its own docstring already promises it and /runs/{id}/summary proves it unenforced), the implemented-and-uncalled register over __all__ exports, and the computed-but-unprinted test over every distinct calculation name a run records. These are the only durable defence against the next instance of the defect this whole programme is about, and they fail the build rather than waiting for an audit.

The single named primary bar — verifiability ≥4 of 6, against 0 of 9 — with three supporting numbers beside it. One clean bar on the dimension where the evidence is already on disk is better than a compound target, and it is the dimension the platform exists for.

The explicit narrowing of three claims the product should stop making (speed, news recency, the UK) versus the one it should defend without compromise (the view, as the operator's own judgement). 'A tool that asks a human to approve six gates cannot beat a tool that asks nothing, on minutes, ever' — say that on the request form rather than chasing it.
The recomputation that honours the A/B swap on the azn round — the only plan that noticed the assignment is not fixed across comparisons.

scores.synthesisAdvice:
SPINE: the document-first plan (Plan 1), for three operator reasons. It is the shortest at 43 sessions and cheapest at £43, so it is the one I would actually finish. Its step-7 steer buys the answer to "is this better than the console?" for £10.50 after nineteen sessions, with the three possible readings written down in advance — no other plan puts a real decision that early or that cheaply. And its ordering is the only one argued from the record rather than from taste: azn2 already ran the experiment of fixing the numbers and stating a view without fixing the self-contradiction, and changed no verdict, which is exactly why the view sits fourth.

The journey-first plan (Plan 2) is a genuine tie on points and loses only on finishability. Take its arguments even where you do not take its order.

GRAFT, in the order I would land them:

1. INTO STEP 1, from Plan 2 and Plan 4 — three questions settled before any code. (a) Does the audit's five-run database and artefact store still exist? Plan 1 has at least four exit criteria and its entire £0 offline economy resting on "re-render msft1 and mtb from their stored rows", and never asks. If the answer is no, buy one seeding run now and say so. (b) What does the executed EODHD agreement actually permit in an exported artefact? `fetch/policy.py:192` and `render/document.py:436` currently disagree, and three of Plan 1's W3/W5 items are designed on the side that loses. Write the answer into one place everything reads. (c) Plan 2's "replay-first rule" into CONTRIBUTING.md — a document change ships with an offline proof; a live run is spent only on what no stored run can exercise. That rule is what makes £43 possible at all.

2. INTO STEP 2, from Plan 3 — its "four counters that count the wrong thing", as one sitting. The turnover guard queries `total_assets` where the canonical concept is `assets` (I verified the branch is unreachable from the gate); the price step reports "the provider returned no prices" when it means no new bars were inserted, which voids the entire price-derived layer on any warm database and would silently make every re-measurement after the first measure a different product; the runtime estimate sums overlapping steps; two docstrings state counts the code contradicts. Also take Plan 3's one-page note on what can actually refuse a run — `vertical_slice_v1.py:1659` says "scores, never a pause", and eleven diagnosis items assume otherwise.

3. INTO STEP 2, from Plan 4 — the three standing tests (route-reachability, implemented-and-uncalled, computed-but-unprinted). They cost little, they fail the build, and they are the only thing in any plan that stops this class of defect recurring. Plan 1 has no structural defence of its own thesis.

4. PROMOTE THE BANK out of Plan 1's optional branch and into a step of its own, roughly at Plan 1's step 3, using Plan 2's ordering argument verbatim: withhold at the parse layer FIRST (the one place all six revenue-reading surfaces inherit from), then derive on top, because seven of the eleven impossible relations are quarterly and `analyse_company` builds annual statements only — so a calculation-layer fix clears four of eleven and gate 2 still refuses. Gate it on the free offline FY2021-23 splice before writing any code. This is the audit's one open blocking finding and an entire subject class; it should not be an "optional branch".

5. THICKEN ISSUE 1. Plan 1 gives the journey eight sessions "spread between the live runs", which is the thinnest treatment of the operator's first-named issue in the four. Take Plan 2's dead-end inventory derived from `runs/console.html`'s own panels as well as from §5, take its correction that the re-seal action is a prerequisite of the re-measure action, and build the offline journey harness (fake scene, no network, £0) at Plan 1's step 2 rather than later — it is free, it must be red on today's tree, and it turns every ISSUE-1 fix into a named row going green. Do NOT take Plan 4's placement of this work after M1.

6. INTO STEP 2's judging harness, from Plan 3 — the calibration round. Before any new judged round is believed, re-judge September's committed corpus with the coded panel and require it to reproduce the recorded per-comparison verdicts, with an empty rubric-key diff. One sitting, £7.50, and it is the cheapest possible way to discover the instrument is wrong. Also take Plan 3's discriminating pair (platform MSFT against platform AZN) so you can tell a strong signal from one opinion sampled three times.

7. INTO MEASUREMENT, from Plan 4 — make verifiability ≥4 of 6 the single headline bar, with Plan 1's other thresholds kept as supporting numbers. It is the dimension the platform exists for, it is the one where the evidence is already on disk (259/259 verified, 3,335 rows replayed) and it lost 0 of 9, and one clean bar is easier to hold yourself to than a compound one. Keep Plan 1's insistence that `view_stated` moves to the no-regression list rather than the target list — azn2 already scores 3/3 on it, so it cannot signal a fix.

8. INTO THE PRODUCT DOCUMENTATION, from Plan 4 — narrow the three claims that cannot be defended (speed under time pressure, news recency, the UK), in the product's own words, and defend the fourth (the view, as the operator's own non-binding judgement) without compromise. An hour and a half of honesty removes a dead end and stops the next session building a UK acquisition path.

DISCARD from Plan 3: the five-round, £182.50, 95-session, 25-ADR shape. Its instruments are right and largely appear in the other three plans anyway; its price does not survive contact with one person, one machine and a £100 ceiling that is already £63.32 spent. DISCARD from Plan 4: the placement of WS6, and the 95-session headline — its content is almost all inside Plan 1's workstreams already, expressed more cheaply.

The result is roughly 50 sessions and about £52: Plan 1's spine and steer, with the bank promoted, the journey harness pulled forward, the replay and licence questions settled first, and the calibration round protecting the only instrument that can answer the operator's second question.

fatalFlaws: Effort is roughly half what this tree will demand. 43 sessions for ~90 findings and 14 ADRs, in a 378-file / 119k-line repo where core/ and calc/ are mypy --strict and pure, renderers carry byte-stability pins, and the suite needs one DB per process and two pytest invocations. W5 alone is 12 items in 6 sessions and contains the scale-word rewrite (numerals_in returns a frozenset; making it position-carrying inside pure strict core is its own multi-session job, which the plan's own risk section admits) plus a third evidence category needing an ADR 0058 amendment. W8 is 14 items in 8 sessions 'spread between the live runs'. Expect 70-80.

ISSUE 1 is structurally thin. Only two journey items are prerequisites; the rest is 'fixed on evidence as the runs meet it', and the harness numbers are only taken at the verdict round. If the programme stops at its own stated stop point (step 6 or step 9), half the operator's request is unaddressed.

The bank is an OPTIONAL BRANCH gated on an operator decision. F-24 is the one open blocking finding and no bank produces an approvable report at all; a plan that can run to completion and leave an entire subject class unresearchable has mis-scoped the word 'ready'.
whatToGraft: The step-7 live steer: one AZN run plus 3 reads and 3 comparisons for £10.50, placed after six offline steps, with the reading pre-registered three ways (moved off contradiction/price/view = ordering right; still naming header or accusations = implementation bug; naming neither = thesis wrong, reorder). This is the best-placed and cheapest decision gate in the whole set and every other plan should adopt it.

The dependency argument for putting the two recovery items (superseding AMENDED decision, re-measure/re-seal) at step 2 rather than in the ISSUE-1 block: a document-first programme changes things and re-runs, and re-running is exactly what strands a run. Plans 3 and 4 schedule paid rounds before this work and are exposed to a 3-of-6 base rate.

The measurement discipline of demoting view_stated to the no-regression list because azn2 already scored it 3/3 — a bar the platform already clears cannot signal a fix.

'Report at gate 2 for two clean live runs, then promote to a refusal' for the new cross-section check, with the re-measure/supersede actions built first precisely so a new blocking check cannot strand the programme's own re-runs.

fatalFlaws: The keystone is buried. Porting red_team.py's calculation index into gather_evidence is one session, needs no ADR, no decision and no spend, and removes the defect every one of the nine comparisons named first — and it sits at step 6, behind roughly 14 sessions of bank and recovery work. The plan says so itself ('the cheapest change in the entire plan that a judge would notice') and then schedules it seventh.

Workstream F (16 sessions) is the same optimism the other plans show: a new EDGAR client method plus an index.json parser plus replay fixtures, the _text_of/record_excerpts cache reshape, tier version rows, a nineteenth section definition, the closed-world content fix and the standing scope test is 20+ on this codebase, not 16. Total 65 is closer to honest than plan 1 but still ~20% light.

whatToGraft: The replay-first rule, written into CONTRIBUTING.md and the protocol: a document change ships only with an offline proof (re-render from a stored run, aer replay-draft, aer rehearse-section); a live run is spent only on what no stored run can exercise. This is the single best cost-control mechanism in the set and it belongs in the winner verbatim.

Step 1's question nobody else asks: do the audit's five run databases and artefact store still exist? Eleven acceptance criteria across these plans assume `aer replay-draft <job-id>` against those jobs. If they are gone, a large fraction of every plan's 'verified offline at £0' becomes a £7 lesson. Settle it before scheduling anything.

The correction list, which is the most useful engineering content in any of the four: an eval metric cannot pause a run; evaluate_run is not model-free (verified — it takes AgentContext and use_batch); Cost.agent_run_id foreign-keys an uncommitted agent_runs row so 'publish cost early' means publishing agent_runs early too; discover_documents builds refs from primary documents only and cannot enumerate an accession; the re-seal action is a PREREQUISITE of the re-measure action because re-scoring always moves the live payload off the frozen seal (the diagnosis has that dependency backwards).
Correctly numbered ADRs from 0113 — verified, 112 exist — with each one naming the ADR it amends. Plans 1 and 4 use letters and descriptions, which is one more translation step at execution time.

Making the bank mandatory and early, with the FY2021-23 splice run offline as the gate before any code (3,825+2,167=5,992; 5,822+2,357=8,179; 7,115+2,528=9,643), and the parse-layer-first ordering argued from mechanism: analyse_company builds annual statements only, so a calc-layer derivation can never clear the seven quarterly plausibility findings and can never on its own reach gate 2.

The ISSUE-1 test written as concrete counts against concrete September values (34,540 gate-page words, 21 UUIDs, 2/5/3 hand-typed assumptions, 3 of 6 runs approved) — the most operational of the four.

fatalFlaws: The instrument eats the programme. £144.50 of £182.50 total spend is measurement, across four paid rounds, and 15 sessions pass before a single product defect a user meets is fixed. The operator asked for a plan of action to fix two issues; this is a plan to build an observatory and fix things underneath it.

85-95 sessions, 18 steps, 25 new or amended ADRs, driven by one person. This will not complete, and unlike plan 4 it names no coherent stop point where the work so far is a finished product — 'the tranches' are sized to the rounds, not to shippable states.

Sequencing puts M4's scale-word fix at step 5, before any of the document work it protects, and correctly sizes it as hard (numerals_in must become position-carrying inside mypy --strict pure core) — so the plan front-loads one of its most expensive and least judge-visible items. Meanwhile the ISSUE-1 fix tranche (F1, 10 sessions) waits until step 6 and the exported-document work until step 9.
whatToGraft: THE CALIBRATION ROUND. Re-judge September's committed corpus with the newly coded panel and require it to reproduce the recorded per-comparison verdicts before any later round is believed. £7.50, one sitting, and if it fails nothing measured afterwards means anything. No other plan has this and every one of them needs it.

The discriminating pair in every round — the platform's MSFT document against the platform's own AZN document, where the three lenses SHOULD disagree — with the rule that if they never disagree the panel is reported as one opinion sampled three times. Given the raw data (51-3-0 across 54 votes, and would_act unanimous 9/9 in both directions), this is the correct guard against a shared prior.

The one-page note recording what can actually stop a run (the FINAL gate's _refuse_unsupported_evidence raising StepPaused, the degradation path, and the fact that an evaluation row cannot) — written before any work, because eleven diagnosis items propose a refusal through a mechanism that does not exist.

M1's four counters as a single early sitting: the turnover guard's total_assets→assets strings (verified: evaluations.py queries a concept the canonical set does not hold, so the branch has never fired), the inserted-vs-held bars count, the gate-1 estimate that sums overlapping steps, and the two drifting docstring counts. The bars one in particular means every re-measurement after the first would otherwise be measuring a different product on a warm database.

Judge spend recorded through Ledger.record(kind='other', label='judging') and each round's absolute budget asserted against a ledger reading taken at the protocol's own commit — September's judges were off-ledger by construction.

fatalFlaws: M1 is scheduled wrong. Two paid live runs at step 10 sit ahead of WS6 (steps 11-12), which is the workstream that removes the dead ends and gives a stranded run an exit. September's base rate was three of six runs reaching an approved, rendered report; the plan stakes its single go/no-go decision on runs it has not yet made survivable, and its own risk entry admits 'M1's two runs carry the risk knowingly'. Move the three true dead ends and the re-seal/re-measure actions ahead of M1.

ISSUE 1 as a whole lands after the decision gate. WS6 is 16-19 sessions — the largest single workstream — and everything in it is provable offline at £0, so there is no cost argument for deferring it. Half the operator's request is therefore conditional on a measurement of the other half.

£35 at step 15 on peer seeding, behind the plan's own admission that the subject's own P/E and EV/EBITDA may be enough and 'M1 will say'. That is a third of the live budget committed to something the plan flags as possibly unnecessary.
whatToGraft: Step 3 — build the three mechanisms exactly once, before anything routes through them: the gate-2 blocking path distinct from eval metrics, the route-reachability test over the shell registry's UNLISTED set, the implemented-and-uncalled register over __all__ exports, and the ADR 0061 scope test. This is the best piece of platform engineering in the set. I verified the thesis it defends: create_scenario/set_override, margin_bridge and MacroClient have no non-test callers today, and nothing in CI would have caught it.

Step 1's demand to settle the ADR 0030 determination in ONE place before any render change. This is not an operator decision waiting to be taken — the codebase already contradicts itself, with fetch/policy saying derived figures are publishable and render/document enforcing the pre-amendment posture in a type signature (verified: assemble_document takes `comps: WithheldComps | None`). Three of plan 1's and plan 2's items are designed on top of that contradiction without naming it.

Step 2's free unblockers as literally the first code: the evidence query port, the turnover strings, the held-vs-inserted bars, the tier predicate pushed into the query before the cap, the two stale docstrings. Each is an hour to a session and each unblocks something larger.

The standing computed-but-unprinted test — enumerate every distinct calculation name a run records and assert each either reaches a rendered surface or is on a declared working-paper-only list. It is the only durable defence any plan offers against the defect class that produced this audit.

The honesty about the September baseline: it is the only plan that states the A/B swap on the azn round is honoured in its recomputation, which I confirmed is real (A is the baseline document for all three azn comparisons). It also picks verifiability as the PRIMARY bar, which is right — it is the dimension the platform exists for, lost 0 of 9 (console 6, equal 3), and the material to fix it is already stored and hashed.

Naming what to narrow rather than defend: speed/use-case-7, news recency, and the UK path — with the honest line that a tool asking for six gate approvals cannot beat one that asks nothing, so fix the 22 minutes of silence instead.

scores.synthesisAdvice:
SPINE: the delivery / last-mile plan (plan 4). Its diagnosis is the one I verified as literally true in the tree — the platform computes, stores and hashes far more than it prints — and that reframing changes the work from "build capability" to "connect and render", which is the only reading under which a solo operator finishes anything. It is the only plan that builds shared mechanisms once instead of letting three items each invent a refusal path, the only one that notices fetch/policy and render/document already disagree about ADR 0030, and the only one with a named stop point (steps 1-10, ~45 sessions, ~£29) that is a complete plan with its own measurement. Adopt its workstream boundaries and its step 1-3 opening verbatim.

FIX THE SPINE'S ONE SCHEDULING ERROR FIRST. Move plan 1's step-2 recovery prerequisites — the superseding Decision.AMENDED at a stale gate, the re-measure action, the re-seal action (in that dependency order: re-seal enables re-measure, per plan 2's correction), and the decided-gate console state — into plan 4's step 3, ahead of any paid run. Then move the rest of WS6 from steps 11-12 to immediately after WS1, because all of it is provable on the fake scene at £0 and it is half the operator's request. Nothing in WS2-WS5 depends on it, so it costs only calendar.

REPLACE M1 WITH PLAN 1'S STEP-7 STEER. Plan 4's M1 is two runs and £21; plan 1's steer is one AZN run, 3 reads and 3 comparisons for £10.50, on the one subject where the thesis has already half-failed (azn2 scored view_stated 3/3 and argued 3/3 and still lost 3/3). Take plan 1's three pre-registered readings of that result, which convert a gate into an actual branch instead of a vote of confidence. Keep plan 4's verifiability-≥4-of-6 as the primary bar and plan 1's exclusion of view_stated to the no-regression list.

GRAFT THE INSTRUMENT FROM PLAN 3, NOT ITS SCHEDULE. Take exactly three things: the calibration round (re-judge September's committed corpus with the coded panel and require reproduction of the recorded verdicts before believing any later round — £7.50, and without it two rounds are not comparable), the discriminating pair with the "if the lenses never disagree, report it as one opinion sampled three times" rule, and the one-page note on what can actually stop a run. Leave plan 3's four paid rounds and its £144.50 of measurement behind; two rounds — the £10.50 steer and one verdict round — is the right cadence. Neutral A.md/B.md paths and the identity-guess key are non-negotiable in any round: the September console notes sat under a directory literally named `baseline`, which I confirmed in reads.json, so "nine of nine chose the console" is a result whose blind was never demonstrated.

GRAFT PLAN 2'S ECONOMICS AND ITS CORRECTIONS. Write the replay-first rule into CONTRIBUTING.md before session one: a document change ships with an offline proof, and live money is spent only on what no stored run can exercise. Settle plan 2's step-1 question — do the audit's five run databases and artefact store still exist — before scheduling, because a large fraction of every plan's "£0, verified offline" depends on it. Carry plan 2's corrections into every acceptance criterion: no criterion may name a refusal without naming the code path that refuses; evaluate_run is not model-free so the re-measure-inside-revise item must first carve out a deterministic entry point; Cost.agent_run_id FKs an uncommitted agent_runs row so prefer up-front reservation over early publication; discover_documents cannot enumerate an accession, so EX-99 acquisition is a new client method and an index parser, not a filter. Take plan 2's numbered ADRs from 0113 (112 exist) in place of plan 4's letters, and make the bank mandatory and early with the FY2021-23 splice as the offline gate before any code.

EFFORT: budget 90-110 sessions, not 43 and not 65. Plan 4's ranges are the most honest of the four and are still light on WS7. Three items are systematically under-sized across all four plans and should be re-estimated on contact rather than argued about now: the scale-word hint (numerals_in must become position-carrying inside mypy --strict pure core, touching three set operations in the draft rule), the exhibit-as-table change (a rows field on Chart and ChartView plus both serialisers plus re-pinned byte-stability tests), and the accession/exhibit acquisition path. Keep plan 4's stop point at ~45 sessions and treat everything after the steer as re-argued on what the steer measured.

THE ONE THING NO PLAN SEQUENCES QUITE RIGHT: the licence question raised by printing verified excerpts into an immutable exported artefact. All four flag it; make it a blocking precondition of the export work rather than a note inside it, because `aer purge-licensed` exists specifically because a terminated subscription obliges deletion of stored payloads, and an excerpt copied into a sealed artefact is a payload copy the purge cannot reach.

fatalFlaws: The bank is optional. The audit's own words are that F-24 is the one blocking finding still open and 'until it is taken a bank produces no approvable report'. Making a whole subject class an 'OPTIONAL BRANCH, operator decision' at step 8 means the £9.64 already spent on two MTB runs stays spent for nothing and MTB is never judged. That is not a scope choice, it is declining the one measured hard-blocker.

The justification for deferring all journey work is a hope, and the arithmetic refutes it: 'the journey defects are met, diagnosed and fixed on runs already being paid for'. The plan commissions four live runs. Four walks will not encounter a stale approval, a refused check, a rejected gate, an unreachable Redis and a JSON 500. The dead-end inventory in W8 is explicitly 'kept as a living table... updated' by those four walks — that is discovery-by-luck standing in for the free, offline, fake-scene harness the plan itself builds in W9.

The £43 budget rests on an unverified premise. Steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11 are all costed at £0 on 're-render msft1, azn2 and mtb from their own stored rows'. Nothing in the plan establishes that the audit's five jobs still exist in a live database; the committed evidence is JSON exports and there is no import path. Plans 2 and 4 make this a step-1 question. If the answer is no, this plan's entire cost model and most of its acceptance criteria are unwritable.

'At least 3 of 6 comparisons do NOT choose the console' counts 'equal' as a pass, so a round of six equals clears the primary brief bar. Stated honestly and paired with a hard verifiability bar, but it is the softest headline threshold in the set.
whatToGraft: The ordering argument, which is the single most sceptic-proof reasoning anywhere in the four: azn2 scored view_stated 3/3 and argued 3/3 and still drew 'no' from 3 of 3 — therefore the view goes fourth, not first. Every plan that puts the view early is arguing against a measured null result.

The explicit exclusion of view_stated from the target list, moved to no-regression, on the stated ground that 'a bar the platform already clears cannot signal a fix'. This is the anti-gaming discipline the whole programme needs.

The step-7 LIVE STEER: one AZN run at £10.50 after six offline steps, on the one subject where the thesis has already been half-tested and failed, with the reading pre-registered three ways (moved off contradiction / still on the header / neither). Cheapest honest kill-check in the set, and positioned ~24 sessions earlier than Plan 4's equivalent.
The notDoing discipline, especially the UK paragraph: name the seven-to-ten-session cost, refuse it, and spend ninety minutes making the product stop selling the dead end instead.

The gate-promotion rule: ship the cross-section check as a gate-2 report, promote to refusal only after two consecutive clean live runs, so a new blocking check cannot strand the programme's own re-runs.

fatalFlaws: The mid-point signal at step 9 does not test what it claims. Re-rendering MSFT #1 and AZN #2 from stored records under new code produces a document whose evidence pack, research findings and adversarial record were all generated by the old code — a document the platform would never actually emit. Judging it tells you about the renderer, not about the run. The £11 live MSFT run is bolted on beside it rather than being the thing judged. That weakens the plan's own answer to its strongest objection.

The primary ISSUE-2 bar is argued down before the result is known, with a pre-built excuse attached: 'I recommend 3 of 6 because the console's advantage on argument is partly a format-expectation effect this plan does not fully address'. A threshold chosen with its own exculpation already written is a threshold designed to be cleared. Plan 4 sets the harder bar on the one dimension where the evidence is already on disk, which is the correct shape.

Fifteen steps and ~65 sessions before the only instrument that can answer ISSUE 2 runs at full strength. The plan is honest that this is its central risk, but the mitigation (above) does not carry the weight placed on it.
whatToGraft: The bank at step 2, and the withhold-then-derive ordering with the reason that makes it load-bearing rather than stylistic: seven of the eleven impossible relations are quarterly, `analyse_company` builds annual statements only, so a calculation-layer fix clears 4 of 11 and gate 2 still refuses; the parse layer at companyfacts.py:199-235 is the one place all six revenue-reading surfaces inherit from. This is the sharpest single correction to the audit's own sizing in any of the four plans, and it is gated on a free offline splice that must reproduce three reported years exactly before a penny moves.

The replay-first rule written into CONTRIBUTING.md and the protocol: a document change ships with an offline proof; a live run is spent only on what no stored run can exercise. This is what makes any document programme affordable, and Plan 1 assumes it without writing it down.

The step-1 question 'do the audit's five run databases and artefact store survive?', with the stated consequence that the answer decides whether the programme costs £34 or £60. Every plan's offline acceptance criteria hang on it.
The dependency correction that the re-seal action is a prerequisite of the re-measure action, because re-scoring always moves the live payload off the frozen seal.

The mechanism corrections used as sizing inputs rather than footnotes: `evaluate_run` is not model-free, `Cost.agent_run_id` FKs an uncommitted `agent_runs` row, `discover_documents` cannot enumerate an accession, `numerals_in` returns a frozenset so the scale-word fix must become position-carrying inside mypy --strict core.

fatalFlaws: Proportion. £182.50 and 85-95 sessions, with a request to raise CEILING_GBP to £190, for one private investor's personal tool that produces one report at a time against an audited £100 ceiling with £36.68 of residue. Four formal measurement rounds at £31.50 each is more instrument than the thing being measured warrants, and Rounds 1 and 2 share most of their content — the attribution they buy is real but it is not worth £63 plus twelve judged reads twice over.

Fifteen sessions and four steps pass before one defect a user actually meets is fixed. The plan concedes this in its own risk list and answers it with 'three of those five steps cost nothing live' — which is about money, not about the operator's months. A measurement programme that has not yet fixed anything is the failure mode the audit's §4.1 already demonstrated in mirror image: fifteen green metrics on documents six judges refused to act on.

The permanent-metric promotion carries a real cost the plan under-books: moving `numerals/facts/match` into src/ means a ruff/mypy migration of 1,284 exempted lines with 31 errors including PLR0912/PLR0915, and the plan itself says this is most of the work — then budgets four to five sessions for a metric that ships advisory and cannot block anything until a mutation corpus exists.
whatToGraft: THE CALIBRATION ROUND. Re-judge September's committed corpus with the coded panel and require it to reproduce the recorded per-comparison verdicts before any later round is believed. £7.50, one sitting, and if it fails nothing measured afterwards means anything. This is the best single idea in all four plans and the other three omit it entirely.

The 'four counters that count the wrong thing' tranche as a named prerequisite: the turnover guard querying a concept that does not exist (verified — evaluations.py:612,646 vs core/concepts.py:110), the bars count that voids the price layer on any warm database, the gate-1 estimate that sums overlapping steps and produced the audit's published 31-42 against a true merged 26.5-36.8, and the drifting docstrings. Fix the instrument's own bugs before the instrument measures anything.

The one-page note recording what can actually stop a run — the FINAL gate's evidence rule raising StepPaused, the degradation path, and the fact that an eval row cannot — written before any acceptance criterion names a refusal. Eleven diagnosis items proposed refusals through a mechanism that does not exist.

The correction that the September completeness scorer scores azn2 `market_capitalisation: true` off the sentence 'no market capitalisation was available'. The readout must be built from the run's own rows and treated as a correction to the old scorer, never as a target to reproduce.

The mutation corpus as the condition for promoting `filing_agreement` past advisory: it was calibrated to zero on the very reports it would gate and its recall has never been measured, so recall must be a number before the blocking question is even asked.
The discriminating pair in every round (the platform's MSFT against the platform's own AZN) as a test that the three lenses are three opinions rather than one sampled three times.

fatalFlaws: ISSUE 1 waits behind roughly 45 sessions of document work, and the plan's own framing refutes the delay: it says ISSUE 1 'is a count, not an opinion', that the fake scene drives the whole workflow for £0 with no network, and that three inventory rows start red. There is no evidence-based reason to put the free, offline, immediately-scoreable half of the operator's request after the expensive, judge-dependent half. This is the mirror of Plan 1's flaw and it costs the operator the one deliverable they could have in a fortnight.

The 'about sixty of those sessions are connecting, correcting or printing something that already exists' claim is the plan's own thesis applied to its own estimate, and it does not hold for WS7. Acquiring EX-99 needs a new EDGAR client method, an index.json parser and a replay fixture; the tier ceiling is a policy decision with new version rows and claim-level marking; peer acquisition is an ADR 0059 amendment plus the containment condition ADR 0061 exists to prevent. Those are builds, not connections, and they are 18-22 of the sessions.

95 sessions and £108 for a solo operator. The plan mitigates this properly by making steps 1-10 a complete self-contained plan with its own gate, but the headline number is still the second largest in the set and the conditional tail is where most of the reach work lives.
whatToGraft: The A/B swap correction, stated in the open: 'September's true baseline, recomputed from judges/reads.json with the A/B swap on the azn round honoured'. I verified this independently — an uncorrected tally gives console 34 / equal 3 / platform 17, which would materially understate the loss. Only this plan shows its working. Any protocol built on reads.json must carry this correction as a test.

The three standing tests that defend the plan's own thesis against recurrence: route-reachability over the shell registry's UNLISTED set, the implemented-and-uncalled register over __all__ exports, and the computed-but-unprinted test over every distinct calculation name a run records. Six complete tested modules are already called from nowhere; nothing today catches the seventh. This is the only structural guard against the failure mode in the set.
Building the gate-2 blocking path ONCE, in step 3, before three items route through it — rather than each workstream inventing its own refusal.

Settling the ADR 0030 licence question by re-reading the executed agreement and writing the answer into one place everything reads, on the ground that fetch/policy.py:176-192 and render/document.py currently disagree. Every plan designs price-figure items on top of that contradiction; only this one names it as a step-1 fact to establish rather than a decision to take.

The three claims to narrow (speed, news recency, the UK) and the one to defend without compromise (the view as the operator's own judgement). It is the clearest statement of what the product should stop claiming, which is itself an ISSUE-1 fix.

M1 as a genuine kill-gate with verifiability as the primary bar, justified by a falsifiable prediction — 'the one dimension where the evidence is already on disk and where I would predict a clean flip' — with the money gated on testing it.

scores.synthesisAdvice:
SPINE: the delivery-first plan. Its reframing is the only one that is itself a measured claim rather than an interpretation — six complete, tested, uncalled modules, a render signature enforcing a licence position the operator reversed, one ORDER BY that starves the arguing sections — and it is the only plan that builds standing tests against its own thesis recurring. It handled the judges' data most carefully (it is the only plan that names the azn A/B swap, which I verified: uncorrected the tally reads console 34 / platform 17, corrected it reads 51 / 0). Keep its step 1-3 shape, its M1 kill-gate with verifiability as the primary bar, and its explicit list of claims to narrow.

THEN MAKE FOUR CHANGES, each taken from another plan, each because the record says so:

1. MOVE ISSUE 1 IN FRONT OF THE DOCUMENT WORK. Take journey-first's steps 1-5 and put them before the spine's WS1. The spine's own words are that ISSUE 1 is a count, that the fake scene drives the whole workflow for £0 with no network, and that three inventory rows start red — so the half of the operator's request that needs no judge and no money is being made to wait 45 sessions behind the half that needs both. Build the dead-end inventory and the harness first, prove it RED, then turn rows green. Reject document-first's contrary argument outright: four live runs cannot walk six stopped states, so 'fix the journey while the runs are in flight' is a hope, not a plan.

2. PUT THE BANK SECOND, WITH JOURNEY-FIRST'S ORDERING ARGUMENT INTACT. F-24 is the only blocking finding the audit left open and an entire subject class produces no approvable report; document-first makes it optional, which is the worst call in the set. Take withhold-at-the-parse-layer-then-derive, with the reason that makes the ordering load-bearing (seven of eleven findings are quarterly, analyse_company is annual-only, so deriving clears 4 of 11 and gate 2 still refuses), gated on the free offline FY2021-23 splice reproducing to the pound before a line of code. Ship the `total_assets`→`assets` fix beside it — I confirmed the guard is unreachable, so it adds two findings before it removes thirteen.

3. GRAFT MEASUREMENT-FIRST'S CALIBRATION ROUND AND COUNTER-FIXES, BUT NOT ITS PROPORTION.
